summary: Substrate subsumption risk: MODERATE-TO-HIGH and rising — Anthropic publicly frames "self-learning agents" as roadmap (Dreaming, Code with Claude May 2026). ALREADY SUBSUMED: task deps/claiming, routing smarts, loop pacing, token budgets (Task Budgets API beta), agent-isolation worktrees. PARTIAL: cross-session task sharing (CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, opt-in/no union), memory consolidation (Dreams = cloud-only batch over markdown stores, no graph/no execution coupling), escalation (teams plan-approval). DURABLE: metric/judge/benchmark optimize loop (nothing native measures whether output improved), bi-temporal note/supersede knowledge graph wired to execution, cross-workspace ghost edges, local-neutral daemon posture. New risk found: cleanupPeriodDays sweep now garbage-collects ~/.claude/tasks/, invalidating our "native persistence is indefinite" assumption — snapshot native fields into overlay at completion. Deliberate substrate-ride deletions listed (router smarts, loop plumbing, generic worktree mgmt). Full report: /Users/imyu/Desktop/cloude/scratch/competitive/B3-substrate-risk.md

item.value: Anthropic shipped 'Dreaming' (Managed Agents API, beta header dreaming-2026-04-21, research preview): async job reads a memory store + up to 100 session transcripts, outputs a NEW deduped/reorganized memory store. Cloud-only, batch, markdown stores — NOT a graph, NOT execution-coupled, NOT in local Claude Code. Direct conceptual overlap with our judge dup-cluster consolidation; the worst direction-signal for our self-learning moat.

CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID env var makes multiple Claude Code sessions on one machine share a single task list (same storage dir, real-time file-watch sync). Opt-in per session at launch, no union of pre-existing lists, no cross-list deps, same-machine only (source: claudearchitect.com, third-party/unofficial). Partially subsumes our cross-session graph pillar; one Anthropic default-flip to per-workspace lists would reduce lib/native-tasks.js aggregation to a thin shim.

GOTCHA: Claude Code changelog (~2.1.118) says the cleanupPeriodDays retention sweep now ALSO covers ~/.claude/tasks/. The orchestrator README's verified assumption 'native task persistence is durable and indefinite, no copy needed' is now WRONG — native truth under long-lived graph nodes can be garbage-collected. Mitigation: snapshot native task fields into the overlay/git substrate at completion. Also: agent-team task dirs ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/ are deleted at team cleanup by design.

Native auto-memory (CC v2.1.59+) loads MEMORY.md's first 200 lines/25KB WHOLESALE into every session — the philosophical opposite of our abstain-by-default context gate. No temporal/supersede semantics, no semantic search, no task coupling, machine-local per repo. Durable differentiation axes vs native: per-fact bi-temporal supersede, retrieval-gated injection calibrated on measured regret, and knowledge wired by edges to execution.

Subsumption verdict by capability (June 2026): ALREADY SUBSUMED — task deps/claiming, routing smarts (model proposes teams itself), loop pacing + token budgets (Task Budgets API beta task-budgets-2026-03-13, Workflow budgets), agent-isolation worktrees. PARTIAL — cross-session graph (env-var sharing), memory consolidation (Dreams=cloud), escalation (teams plan-approval). DURABLE — metric/judge/benchmark optimize loop (nothing native measures whether output got BETTER), bi-temporal knowledge graph coupled to execution, cross-workspace ghost edges, local-neutral daemon. Bet on: 'the graph that remembers what worked, proves it with numbers, feeds it forward'.

Ride-the-substrate deletions identified (less surface = win): (1) freeze router classifier smarts — keep only orch-gate policy; (2) shed loop interval/budget bookkeeping where /loop, crons, Routines, Task Budgets cover it; (3) keep lib/git.js worktrees ONLY for measure/merge (native EnterWorktree + Workflow isolation handle agent isolation); (4) keep dup-cluster judge scoped to graph note_nodes, never extend to auto-memory markdown (consolidate-memory skill + Dreaming own that); (5) never build team-internal coordination (teams' shared list + mailbox is better) — our layer starts where the team dir gets deleted.
